note: Teaching repertoire already in the catalogue, with the grade it conventionally sits at in the UK/Canadian graded syllabuses (ABRSM, Trinity, RCM). These are the fixed points the cost model and the grade boundaries are calibrated against: a collection is used rather than a single piece wherever the collection is uniform in level, so one odd edition cannot move the anchor. Grades are the collection's typical level, not a claim about every number in it. A collection that spans several grades anchors nothing and is left out. `least` is the fewest pieces a collection may resolve to and still be the thing this file says is graded at that level. Set from what it resolved to when the boundaries were last calibrated, with room for the catalogue to move: half, and never below one. It exists because a pattern that silently stops matching does not weaken the calibration visibly — it just quietly calibrates against fewer collections than the file claims.
